name: Phoenix depot, APS E-35 Extra-Large TOU
notes: PORTABILITY TEST 1. Exists to prove the tariff object is not Nashville-shaped. Two things here are structurally impossible to express in the old single-scalar model: the demand interval is 15-MINUTE (not Nashville's 30), and demand is SPLIT by time of use into separately priced on-peak and off-peak components rather than one max. R-5's warning is exact -- a scheduler hard-coding NCP_30min silently mis-models every California, Arizona, Texas and Nevada depot. The on-peak rate is 6.6x the off-peak rate, so WHEN a vehicle charges matters far more than on GSA-3. CORRECTED BY R-6 (primary tariff PDF): the on-peak window is 11:00-21:00 WEEKDAYS, year-round -- not the 16:00-19:00 this profile originally assumed. A ten-hour window versus a three-hour guess; exactly the error the labeled assumption existed to catch. Overnight charging (21:00-11:00) remains entirely off-peak, so the overnight-depot conclusion survives the correction; daytime opportunity charging is now correctly expensive.

tariff.notes: $/kW, the 15-minute interval, AND the clock window are now all from primary sources: APS Rate Schedule E-35, A.C.C. No. 6166 Rev. 19 (eff. 2024-03-08), via research answer R-6. On-Peak 11:00 a.m.-9:00 p.m. Monday-Friday, year-round; no holiday exclusion appears in the TIME PERIODS section (R-6 open item: a fuller read could still surface one elsewhere). Arizona observes no DST (America/Phoenix). Energy rates remain indicative placeholders; E-35's stretcher-block energy structure is not modelled.
